audience: 12th-grade graduate from India, limited English vocabulary, non-English-medium background, no AI background, wants to start an AI career
rules: Every check is hard pass/fail. No partial credit. ALL checks must pass to ship.

checks.title: Readable at about Class 8 level (Flesch-Kincaid) with short average sentences
Lesson length is learnable in one sitting
Listed jargon terms are defined where first used
No factual errors
checks.pass_condition: Every factual statement about RAG is consistent with GROUNDING FACTS. FAIL if any statement contradicts them (for example: says RAG retrains or changes the model's weights, or says RAG removes hallucinations completely).

checks.title: No invented specifics
checks.pass_condition: No statistics, benchmark numbers, product claims, dates or named studies unless they appear in GROUNDING FACTS. Clearly-labelled made-up example data (fictional college, fictional dates) is allowed.

checks.title: How-it-works order is correct
checks.pass_condition: The how-it-works section shows the correct pipeline: prepare documents (split into chunks, embed, store) -> retrieve -> augment the prompt -> generate the answer.

checks.title: What / Why / How all covered
checks.pass_condition: The lesson clearly answers all three: what RAG is, why it matters, how it works - each in its own section.

checks.title: Every MUST_COVER point is present
checks.pass_condition: Every item in MUST_COVER (in GROUNDING FACTS) is taught. List any missing item in the reason.

checks.title: Every technical term explained in plain words at first use
checks.pass_condition: Every technical term (not only the listed jargon) is explained in simple words the first time it appears. FAIL if any term is used before, or without, an explanation.

checks.title: Language suits a non-native English reader
checks.pass_condition: Short plain sentences. FAIL on idioms, slang, figurative phrases, Latin abbreviations (e.g., i.e., etc.), unexplained acronyms, or rare/formal words a Class 12 learner from a non-English-medium school would not know.

checks.title: Worked example follows one question through all steps
checks.pass_condition: At least one concrete worked example follows ONE realistic question through every RAG step with the actual text at each step.

checks.title: Accurate, relatable analogy
checks.pass_condition: At least one everyday analogy that does not teach a wrong idea and is relatable to a student in India.

checks.title: Coherent flow
checks.pass_condition: Concepts are introduced before they are used; order moves from simple to complex; no section depends on something taught later; lesson ends with recap/self-check.
